en.r: Vale da Morte National Park is a national park in the United States. It covers 13,650 km² and has been protected since 1994. Under the IUCN system it is category II, the national park category: it protects whole ecosystems and welcomes visitors.
en.h: The Timbisha Shoshone have lived in the valley for centuries. The name came from 1849 gold seekers who got stuck here on their way to California. Borax was mined in the 1880s with the famous 20-mule teams. National monument in 1933, national park on 31 October 1994.
en.ff: It is the hottest, driest and lowest US national park: Badwater lies 86 m below sea level, and 56.7 °C was recorded here. Even so it has dunes, canyons, salt flats, endemic pupfish in springs and spectacular wildflower blooms in wet years.
